name: Dichondra

project_scope.region: Central Texas, Hays County and nearby
project_scope.note: Genus-level teaching paired with installed Carolina ponyfoot and D. recurvata cards. Other Dichondra taxa including introduced micrantha may occur; status not inferred from genus alone.

look_here_first: Think TINY morning-glory relative hiding UNDER COIN-SHAPED LEAVES. Look for alternate reniform/heart-notched smooth leaves on long petioles and thin creeping, rooting runners. Seek tiny pale five-lobed flowers and later furry, 2-lobed capsules held by persistent 5-part sepals.

shared_traits: Creeping perennial herbs, often rooting at nodes and making small mats.
Leaves alternate, simple, heart/kidney/round-shaped, entire margins, petioles commonly longer than the tiny flower stalks.
Axillary flowers usually solitary, whitish/greenish and very small, with five fused petal lobes and a five-part persistent calyx.
Mature fruit usually a little two-lobed capsule, not a daisy's awned cypsela or a frogfruit inflorescence.
A full mature specimen allows inspecting petiole hairiness, pedicel recurvature, relative sepal/fruit length and leaf dimensions.
shared_genus_recognition.caution: 'Round leaf' is only genus-level evidence. Characters separate the several accepted North American Dichondra species; the straight vs curved mature fruit stalk and persistent sepal/fruit lengths matter more than size/color alone.

study_strategy.look_here_first: Follow runner → alternate leaf at each node → small green 5-lobed flower under leaf → fruit + five persistent sepals → determine whether flower stalk bends backward.
priority: 01 Find creeping runners through turf; don't assume similar kidney-shaped leaves all belong to Dichondra.
02 Trace actual leaf nodes: one leaf per node (alternate), smooth leaf margin and basal notch at stalk attachment.
03 Search beneath blades for tiny five-lobed cream/green flowers instead of looking for morning-glory funnels.
04 At fruiting season, photograph full pedicel and persistent sepals so you can compare carolinensis versus recurvata.
05 Recurved fruit stalk + larger leaves point toward recurvata/micrantha group; straight stalk + longer sepals favor carolinensis.
study_strategy.warning: Mowed or sterile mats cannot safely be keyed to species from one leaf photograph. Check for cultivated 'Dichondra repens' marketing, which is not an exact local taxonomic identification.

genus_diagnostics.habit: Prostrate/creeping and rooting at nodes, often in thin lawn patches and open soil.
genus_diagnostics.leaves: Alternate, kidney/heart-shaped to round, entire margins; palmate veins from basal notch; size and hair vary substantially by species.
genus_diagnostics.flowers: Very small singly axillary, five-lobed fused corolla with five green persistent calyx sepals, usually under leaf canopy.
genus_diagnostics.fruit: Two lobed dry capsule; calyx persists around developing fruit. Need organ-close images to separate close taxa.
genus_diagnostics.field_caution: Convolvulaceae is not always a showy vine or funnel flower; Dichondra is a low subtle-flowered member.

quick_key.if: Leaves OPPOSITE and margins toothed with tiny yellow daisy-like composite heads
Leaves OPPOSITE with pale button-shaped flowering spikes on long bare stalks
Leaves round, scalloped and petiole attached toward middle of underside; flowers in umbels
Alternate entire kidney leaves, very small pale flower and a straight/barely nodding fruiting stalk; sepals longer than fruit
Alternate reniform often larger leaves, stalk markedly recurved near tip; sepals relatively shorter
quick_key.then: Dichondra recurvata (also compare introduced D. micrantha)

quick_key.if: Leaves densely grey-silvery, especially from dense surface hairs
quick_key.then: Dichondra argentea / other silvery ponyfoot: verify species

comparison_cards.title: Carolina ponyfoot vs Texas D. recurvata
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Check a complete MATURE fruiting pedicel, not just leaf diameter.

field_matrix.recurvata: Sepals shorter or only slightly longer than fruit

comparison_cards.caution: D. micrantha is introduced to Texas and can share recurved pedicels; do not identify every recurved stalk as D. recurvata without fruit/sepal measurements and provenance.

comparison_cards.title: Dichondra vs straggler daisy
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Opposite toothed leaves + yellow floret head means straggler daisy; alternate kidney leaves + solitary greenish cup flower means Dichondra.

comparison_cards.title: Dichondra vs frogfruit
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Frogfruit has opposite foliage and a raised button of little pale flowers; Dichondra has alternate smooth reniform leaves and separate hidden tiny flowers.
